subject: Modify continuous20 experiment: eliminate sample-order confound before GPU use
body: I accept the question but reject the current execution spec as a clean isolation. The staged20 reference did NOT see rows0-159 under one global shuffle: step4 shuffled rows0-31, then cont4+8 shuffled rows32-95, then cont12+8 shuffled rows96-159, each with seed/data_seed 20261001. A fresh continuous160 dataset with shuffle_dataset=true will produce a different global example order. That confounds optimizer/scheduler continuity with sample order. Modify before GPU use: reconstruct/freeze the exact effective staged microbatch order (three deterministic stage-local sampler orders concatenated), then feed the continuous candidate that exact order while preventing any second trainer shuffle. Keep one optimizer/scheduler instance, 20 updates, BNB8, runtime A, zero warmup if the purpose remains isolating staged-reset semantics. Persist ordered record_ids + SHA and prove each 0-159 row occurs exactly once. The fresh rows448-511 one-time panel and prereg NLL/family gates are otherwise accepted. Also state explicitly that this test answers continuous-vs-reset development semantics, NOT the final warmup3/6250-step schedule itself. Do not run GPU until the order binding is frozen/tested and ACKed. If exact staged order cannot be reconstructed mechanically, propose a simpler alternative rather than hand-waving equivalence.
